---
title: "Database-backed binomial and Poisson models"
format: html
execute:
  eval: false
---

`dbglm()` fits ordinary binomial complementary-log-log, logit and probit models,
and log-link Poisson count models, on a
native DuckDB or Databricks relation. Observations, working predictors, and projections stay
in the database; R solves the retained-slope system and, when within configured
limits, sparse two-way FE systems from bounded sufficient statistics. The
weighted statistics are rebuilt at each IRLS iteration.

```r
library(dbreg)
m <- dbglm(
  exit ~ outside_wage + career_value |
    schedule_cell + district + Experience + AGE + SEX + FTPTWK,
  conn = con, table = "risk_set",
  family = binomial("cloglog"), vcov = ~district,
  row_id = c("teacher", "year"), sample_table = "retained_keys"
)
coef(m)
sqrt(diag(vcov(m)))
logLik(m)
glance(m)
```

The caller supplies the intended risk set. `dbglm()` filters missing/nonfinite
model inputs and nonpositive weights, then recursively removes fixed-effect
singletons and all-zero/all-one binomial outcome groups (all-zero groups for
Poisson) before discovering categorical
levels. `fixef_rm` selects `"perfect_fit"` (default), `"singletons"`,
`"infinite_coef"`, or `"none"`. If the selected policy leaves a known infinite
fixed-effect coefficient, fitting errors. These checks do not certify absence
of general regressor-induced separation.

A supplied `row_id` must be unique and nonmissing in the input snapshot.
`sample_table` creates a new temporary relation containing retained source keys
on a caller-owned connection. It never overwrites an existing table. With no
supplied key, a snapshot-local opaque key is assigned once. Models retain counts
and provenance rather than individual rows or database handles. The caller owns
an explicitly exported key relation.

Column names after `|` denote categorical fixed effects even when stored as
numbers. `district^year` denotes one joint effect. District intercepts plus
continuous slopes use `district[yr]` or `district[yr, yr2]`; the trend columns
must already exist in the source. `x:factor(Experience)` without an `x` main
effect estimates direct slopes for every identified experience level. The same
source column can be continuous elsewhere in the formula.

```r
heterogeneous <- dbglm(
  exit ~ outside_wage:factor(Experience) + career_value:factor(Experience) |
    schedule_cell + district + Experience + AGE + SEX + FTPTWK,
  conn = con, table = "risk_set", vcov = ~district
)
trends <- dbglm(
  exit ~ outside_wage |
    schedule_cell + district[yr, yr2] + Experience + AGE + SEX + FTPTWK,
  conn = con, table = "risk_set", vcov = ~district
)
```

Offsets and original weights name source columns. Original weights currently
must be nonnegative integer frequencies; iteration-specific working weights are
fractional. `vcov` accepts `"iid"`, `"hc1"`, or one cluster formula. Inference
uses the normal distribution and explicit fixest-style small-sample corrections.
`n_params_model` and `n_params_vcov` distinguish likelihood and covariance
parameter counts. Defaults follow the tested fixest convention, including its
approximate FE parameter count; `K.exact=TRUE` is unsupported. For base `glm`
covariance comparisons, use `ssc = list(K.adj = FALSE)`.

The inner solver verifies the original weighted group equations. With at most
4,096 FE basis columns it transfers bounded FE cross-products to R and solves
on a structural basis fixed under original weights. Larger systems use
preconditioned conjugate gradients on FE-level coefficients. Corrections are
reconstructed from group lookups, preserving the additive FE span.
The outer solver dampens the full model predictor, requires deviance and score
convergence, and recomputes final projected information and scores. Controls
separate outer, projection, rank and step-halving tolerances. Loss of information
or failed convergence produces an error rather than successful inference.

No-FE models support outcome-free link and response prediction, with saved
categorical levels and fitted offsets. Absorbed new-row prediction is deferred.

```r
promotion <- dbglm(promoted ~ Experience + I(Experience^2) + spine + sex,
                   conn = con, table = "transitions", family = binomial("logit"),
                   ssc = list(K.adj = FALSE))
predict(promotion, newdata = profiles, type = "response")
```

Some promotion designs have a top category that cannot advance. That category
has zero events, so its ordinary logit coefficient has no finite MLE. Different
solvers can report different finite stopping points while returning nearly
identical probabilities. The default errors at numerical probability boundaries.
Explicit `separation = "prediction"` allows a warned no-FE boundary approximation;
`finite_mle` and `converged` are false, and SEs, tests and AIC/BIC are unavailable.
This mode supplies probabilities, not ordinary coefficient inference.

DuckDB and Databricks are supported. Databricks requires a native-query DBI
connection preserving a single session with physical temporary-table support.
Its SQL fallback uses `dbreg.spark_ap_chunk_cycles` window batches; the default
sparse path transfers only bounded FE summaries and checks the same normalized
equations. Short expressions use temporary views while working row state stays
materialized. The Poisson likelihood constant transfers a count histogram capped
at one million distinct counts. Default DuckDB connections are
in memory with spilling disabled. Caller connections retain their configuration
and remain open. Grouped binomial responses, fractional original weights,
categorical no-intercept designs, other families and multi-way clustering are
not implemented. No frailty or EM estimator is included.
